report: PulseSoc Native — App Store Rejection Risk Register
working_tree: DIRTY (uncommitted changes present, including in mobile-native/src)
published_app_store_version: UNKNOWN — no App Store Connect access from this environment

risks.evidence: All build configurations use CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY = "Apple Development" / "iPhone Developer". No "Apple Distribution" identity, no App Store provisioning profile, no PROVISIONING_PROFILE_SPECIFIER anywhere. Release bundle id com.pulsesoc.nativeapp; a separate .dev id and "PulseSoc Native Dev" display name indicate a side-by-side development install workflow.
risks.fix: Configure App Store distribution signing (Apple Distribution cert + App Store provisioning profile) under the team's Apple Developer account. Requires account access — cannot be done from this environment.
risks.verification: Xcode Organizer archive validates with distribution profile.

risks.evidence: aps-environment = development. A TestFlight/App Store build must use production APNs; development entitlement breaks push in distribution builds. The app depends on push (expo-notifications, notification routing).
risks.fix: Use aps-environment = production for the Release/distribution build. Because a single entitlements file is shared across Debug and Release, this needs a Release-specific entitlements file (or build-setting override) so on-device dev push still works. Tied to the distribution setup in R1.
risks.verification: Send a push to a TestFlight build and confirm delivery on device.

risks.evidence: No In-App Purchase SDK present in package.json (no StoreKit bridge, react-native-iap, expo-in-app-purchases, or RevenueCat). Digital premium subscription opens a web billing portal / /pulse/premium via Linking.openURL (premium.ts:101, openPremiumUrl premium.ts:203). Marketplace opens checkout_url/onboarding_url via Linking.openURL (marketplace.ts:227,261).
risks.fix: Digital subscriptions and digital unlocks consumed in-app must use StoreKit IAP. Physical-goods flows must be clearly physical. Until IAP is implemented, disable digital-purchase entry points behind a production flag and update metadata/reviewer notes to not advertise them.
risks.mitigation: Digital-purchase entry points (PremiumScreen purchases, marketplace checkout, seller payout onboarding, course enrollment/teacher/catalog) are now wrapped in DIGITAL_COMMERCE_ENABLED (EXPO_PUBLIC_DIGITAL_COMMERCE_ENABLED, default OFF). No web-payment surface renders in production; underlying web-checkout code is preserved for a future StoreKit build. Does not clear the P0 — StoreKit still required before re-enabling.
risks.verification: Reviewer can complete a StoreKit sandbox purchase; no web checkout for digital goods remains in the submitted binary.
risks.status: OPEN — mitigated (entry points hidden behind flag; StoreKit still required)

risks.evidence: Native project reports 1.0 (build 1) while app.json reports 0.1.0 — mismatch. The 'update existing listing' premise cannot be validated: the published App Store version is unknown from this environment, and multiple src references call the current product 'the WebView app' / 'your current WebView account' (AccountRecoveryScreen.tsx:46, SettingsScreen.tsx:26), suggesting the existing listing may be a web-wrapper rather than this native app.
risks.fix: Read the currently published CFBundleShortVersionString/build in App Store Connect. Set MARKETING_VERSION and CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION greater than every uploaded build. Align app.json. Confirm com.pulsesoc.nativeapp is the existing app record's bundle id.
risks.verification: App Store Connect shows the new version number > published, attached to the existing PulseSoc record.

risks.evidence: ~30 Linking.openURL sites route internal product surfaces (profile, seller store, dashboard, events, creator, growth, learning, calls, account health, live) to the web instead of native screens.
risks.fix: Provide native destinations, or remove/hide the web-escape entry points. Keep only genuinely-external legal pages (already handled as intentional web exceptions in notificationRouting.ts).
risks.mitigation: Duplicate/internal web-escape buttons removed or native-routed across Marketplace, SellerStore, ContentPlanner, GrowthCenter, SellerListingComposer, CreatorStudio, Profile, AlertManagement, IntelligenceCenter, CameraStudio, Courses, and Events (e.g. Events 'Create Live Event' now navigates to native LiveStudio; unused web-fallback helpers/imports removed). Residual escapes limited to: legal/support pages (Apple-exempt), flag-gated commerce (see R3), and a small set of no-native-equivalent fallbacks (intelligence stream cards, CameraStudio unsupported-destination capture/publish, Settings Telegram companion) which are intentionally retained and documented rather than deleted.
risks.verification: Static audit shows no duplicate internal-surface Linking.openURL in the submitted binary except documented legal exceptions and retained no-native-equivalent fallbacks.
risks.status: OPEN — largely mitigated (duplicate/internal escapes removed or native-routed; documented residual fallbacks remain)

risks.affected: mobile-native/app.json (supportsTablet: true), ios/PulseSocNative/Info.plist (iPad orientations incl. landscape)
risks.evidence: supportsTablet: true forces iPad review and iPad screenshots. App is phone-first (portrait, full-bleed phone media); iPad layout is unverified.
risks.fix: Either verify and polish iPad layout + provide iPad screenshots, or set supportsTablet: false to ship iPhone-only.
risks.mitigation: Resolved: app.json supportsTablet set to false and Xcode TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY set to 1 (iPhone-only). No iPad review or iPad screenshots required.
risks.verification: Simulator run on iPad shows no broken layout, or the app is iPhone-only.

risks.evidence: Was generic placeholder: 'Allow $(PRODUCT_NAME) to access your Face ID biometric data.'
risks.fix: Replaced with honest purpose: 'PulseSoc uses Face ID to unlock your saved sign-in securely.' (aligned with app.json).

risks.evidence: Uncommitted changes present, including on-mission web-fallback removals in mobile-native/src/{api/verification.ts, navigation/notificationRouting.ts, screens/VerificationCenterScreen.tsx}. Mission rule: never archive from a dirty/unreviewed tree.
risks.fix: Review, commit, and tag the release candidate before any archive.
risks.verification: git status clean; RC tag present.

risks.evidence: NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypes is an empty array for a social app that collects account info, media, audio, messages, and analytics. Required-reason API declarations (FileTimestamp, UserDefaults, SystemBootTime, DiskSpace) look reasonable.
risks.fix: Confirm the app-level manifest and the App Store Connect App Privacy answers reflect real collection; ensure LiveKit/WebRTC and any analytics SDK manifests are present.
risks.verification: Archive privacy report matches ASC App Privacy answers.

risks.evidence: audio background mode declared. Plausibly justified by LiveKit live/calls, but reviewer note needed.
risks.fix: Keep only if genuinely used; document in reviewer notes.
risks.verification: Audio continues correctly in background during a live/call; no misuse.
